column1: # Feature parity of the two column engines of pg_sift: the index (sift_col) and the table access method (sift_table). One row per feature. Read by scripts/gen-docs.py, which writes
# the table of docs/COL-TAM.md section 13 and fails (--check) when a row disagrees with the source: the seam column names the callbacks of the SiftSrcProvider (src/agg/colsrc.h) the
# feature needs, and a status of works needs every one of them in that engine's provider (src/agg/col.c, src/table/src.c), missing needs none, partial some.
# status: works | partial (not checked against the code) | missing | n/a (the engine has no such thing; the note says why). seam: callbacks joined by +, or - for a feature that is not a callback.
feature
column5: note

column1: Aggregate pushdown (SiftAgg): filters, grouping, aggregates, top-N
column5: the same executor over either source

column1: Per-unit sums, counts, minimum and maximum
column5: exact while the unit has no dead row and its pages are visible (a table: no write buffer row or tombstone in the superblock)

column1: Group histograms (the cube) and calendar cells
column5: a table writes the default cube and the cells of every date and timestamp column; an index takes `preagg` and `calendar_columns`

column1: Minimum and maximum per group of the cube (`cube_minmax`)
column5: a table writes them for the integer measures of its dims (not for calendar cells), as an index does by default; the setting `sift.col_format_minor = 6` writes none

column1: Superunit summaries (`superunit`)
column5: whole-table aggregates read one summary for 16 units on an index; a table has no summaries (it takes the split and span of the key table, not `super`)

column1: Key table of a segment (`key_table`)
column5: a segment answers `WHERE key = x` from one record per key; a table writes it for its foreign key and `*_id` columns, within 3% of a segment, under `sift.table_key_table` (on); only a segment whose superblocks are all plain (no tombstone, write buffer row or uncommitted row) is answered whole

column1: Row counts of a text dictionary (`count_columns`)
column5: `count(*)` of a prefix, a range or an equality of a text column of an index is read from two places of each segment's dictionary; a table writes no counts

column1: Key lists and bitmaps of a leaf (`key_columns`)
column5: a table writes them for its int2, int4 and date foreign key and `*_id` columns that are not unique (the default of an index), within 3% of a unit; `count(DISTINCT)` of a unit that has one reads no row

column1: HyperLogLog sketch (`hll_columns`, `approx_count_distinct`)
column5: `sift.approx_count_distinct` is pushed down and reads the rows; no sketch of the units

column1: Exceptions of a leaf that is NULL in nearly every row (soft-delete stamp)
column5: `IS NULL` / `IS NOT NULL` read the unit's NULL count either way

column1: Rollups of the elements of a list (`rollup_leaves`, paths)
column5: a table keeps the rollups of the lists of its declared paths (`sift.table_set_paths`), written with the units and read by the source of the index; rollups of the rows (`rollup_columns`) are an option of the index

column1: Zone pruning of units by the filters of the statement
column5: range, equality, `IN`, `IS NULL`, `OR` of those

column1: Skip map for parallel morsels
column5: a worker takes ranges of superblocks and begins each, instead of skipping the pruned ones from one map

column1: Parallel scan workers
column5: partitions of a partitioned table too

column1: Partitioned table pushdown
column5: the partitions of one kind (all `sift_table`, or all with a `sift_col` index) are one source; partitions with their columns in another order keep the normal plan

column1: Partition facts kept across statements, pages released between partitions
column5: the facts of a `sift_table` partition are read at each plan, and its source has no release between partitions

column1: Text tests on the encoded form (prefix zones, dictionary codes)
column5: prefix zones skip groups, dictionary codes and encoded strings answer `=`, `<>`, ranges, `IN`, `NOT IN`, `LIKE 'p%'` (a column a group lacks stays with the executor)

column1: Integer comparisons on encoded chunks
column5: the table takes a filter when every segment layout holds the column as an integer leaf (agg/chunkfilter.c)

column1: Decoding only the rows a filter keeps
column5: a unit with few kept rows decodes them, and one the integer filters left few rows is narrowed to them

column1: Decoding straight into the executor's vector
column5: a leaf that is not wide decodes into the executor's buffer in its own type (the read shared with `sift_col`); wide leaves (numeric over 18 digits, interval, enum) decode, then copy

column1: Point directory and heap addresses of a key (`point_columns`, `point_tid_columns`)
column5: a table has no index scan of its own: a btree serves point lookups

column1: Rows of the values of a list (`paths` of a list of strings or numbers)
column5: the point directory of a list's values lists the rows that own each value, exactly; a table has no directory of the elements of a list

column1: Units cut by a key (`key_cut`)
column5: a table has no option surface; a lookup of a key reads the units of its superblocks

column1: Sorted runs and run heads (`order_columns`)
column5: a table writes the run of its timestamp columns where the run takes at most 3% of a unit (a column loaded in order: its rows are the run, and a unit keeps the first and last keys); `ORDER BY .. LIMIT 32` of such a column reads no unit

column1: Run heads of a superblock, read without opening its unit
column5: a superblock of a table may hold write buffer rows and tombstones that its page masks do not show, so the unit is opened

column1: Global order of a leaf (`order_array_columns`)
column5: the sorted `(key, heap address)` entries of every row of a segment; the top-N walks the zones of the units instead

column1: Units read from their end (a key that follows the row order)
column5: ORDER BY key [DESC] LIMIT n over a delta key chunk reads 1,024 rows at a time from the end the sort wants; a sift_table has no chunk that says the order of its keys

column1: Aggregates of a unit net of its dead rows
column5: a VACUUM writes the sidecar of a unit that kept a dead row (a table: `sift_tbl_net_refresh`), valid while the unit has the same dead rows; the rows deleted since are read from the unit

column1: Top-N from the zones of the units
Cache of the top-N walk
column5: the walk is made again by every statement

column1: Top-N on raw uuid and bytea keys
column5: a uuid column is a dictionary of its values; the top-N of uuid and bytea reads the stored codes

column1: Sum and average of a numeric image read from the lanes of each row
column5: the sum adds an integer and a scale made from the lanes of a row, with no dictionary of numerics; a table reads the dictionary

column1: Stored dictionary order (`dict_lookup`)
column5: written for a dictionary of 1,024 strings or more under `sift.table_dict_lookup` (off by default); the top-N of the table reads its byte order

column1: jsonb paths as leaves
column5: `paths` on an index, `sift.table_set_paths` on a table

column1: Shapes that read the heap row again (`set_recheck`)
column5: a table keeps the normal plan for them

column1: Wide types (numeric over 18 digits, interval, enum)
LATERAL, EXISTS and shared CTE rewrites
column5: the planner rewrites apply to a statement over a table

column1: Statistics for the planner (zones, sizes, point and set cover)
column5: a table reports its rows, units and distinct counts, not the zones of its units

column1: Automatic merge and defragmentation
column5: `sift.col_auto_merge`, `sift.table_auto_defrag`

column1: VACUUM, crash recovery, physical replication, upgrade
column5: test/t col_* and tbl_* scripts

column1: Differential tests against the normal plan
column5: coldiff (`--table`), diff_fuzz

column1: GPU kernels (`sift.gpu`)
column5: build option, off by default

column1: Row counts of a range of an integer leaf (`order_array_columns`)
column5: `count(*)` of comparisons of one integer, date or timestamp column of an index is read from the entries between the bounds in the global order of each segment whose units are all exact; a table writes no global order

column1: Row counts between two bounds of a text leaf (`order_array_columns`)
column5: `count(*)` of comparisons of one text column between two bounds is read from the ranks of the strings in the global order of each segment whose units are all exact; a table writes no global order

column1: OFFSET and page filters in the global order (`order_array_columns`)
column5: an `OFFSET` of thousands is cut off the front of the order by counting the entries before a value, a segment that holds only the ends of its order says where they stop, and a condition on another column of a page is tested on the values of the units for the entries known to be exact; a table writes no global order

column1: ORDER BY group, key from the second order (`order_array_group`)
column5: the top-N walks the table of groups of a second order group after group when the group column has no order of its own, and an `OFFSET` is cut by whole groups

column1: A second scan of the same statement
column5: a nested loop that probes the aggregate scan again makes the source ready without opening it again; a table opens it again for each probe

column1: Row counts of one element of a list (point directory of a segment)
column5: `count(*)` of an equality on an element of a text or integer array of an index is the length of the list of the value in the point directory of each segment whose units are all clean and all-visible; a table writes no point directory of elements
